html:
Chahta Yakni, "Choctaw land", was the homeland of the Choctaw in what is now central and southern Mississippi and western Alabama. The Choctaw grew out of the Mississippian chiefdoms of the region and spoke a Muskogean language close to that of the Chickasaw.

  • In 1540 Hernando de Soto fought the chief Tuskaloosa at Mabila, in the region where Choctaw ancestors lived.
  • In the 1700s they were allies of French Louisiana and rivals of the British-backed Chickasaw.
  • In the Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek of 1830 they gave up their last land in Mississippi. They were the first nation removed west under the Indian Removal Act, from 1831; thousands died on the way, and a Choctaw chief is said to have called it a "trail of tears and death".
  • In 1847, hearing of the famine in Ireland, the Choctaw sent money to help the starving.

The Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma descends from those who went west; the Mississippi Band of Choctaw from those who stayed. The map's Choctaw territory shows the nation in later years.
